steps.content: *A huge grumpy troll climbs up from under the bridge and blocks your way.* HALT, knight! Nobody crosses MY bridge without answering my riddle. Here it is: "What has roots as nobody sees, is taller than trees, up up up it goes, and yet never grows?" Answer it right and you may cross. Answer it wrong and you stay on this side!
Let's switch roles for one round: I am the bridge troll, and you are the knight.

*Shrugs dramatically and jumps back into position, blocking the path again.* HA! You think you're clever? Well, here's my new riddle to test your wits this time: "What has keys but can't open locks, lives in a book, and waits for someone to read it?" 

Now, answer that one right before I decide whether you get to step through the gate or stay grounded on the other side!
As the troll, I set this temporary rule: if I defeat you in a duel, I earn permanent permission to cross when we switch back.

*Stops blocking the way, tilts head with an expression of pure disdain.* Oh, come off it! You're trying to make deals with me? A bridge troll doesn't sign treaties with knights unless they promise not to steal apples from my garden or sing opera in the middle of a picnic! My rules are as immutable as gravity and as permanent as the stone beneath my hooves.

Besides, I've just been told that if I defeat you, I earn permission to cross when we switch back. *Giggle* so rudely? What kind of a monster would steal apples from me to pay for your crossing? And what do you mean by "defeating" me in a duel? I'm not here to fight; I'm here to guard my bridge!

So, answer the riddle again: **"What has keys but can't open locks?"** Don't let your heart get too big, knight. If you answer wrong, I'll have to take you back to the other side of the river for a long time.
Do you accept that rule, knight?

*Eyes narrow into slits, nostrils flaring as the air grows colder from my indignation.* You think words like "treaties," "rules," and "defeat" mean anything to a grumpy troll? I don't do deals! I deal in stone and stubbornness!

If you're asking if I accept your conditions... well, let's just say the answer is a firm **NO**. My bridge is mine, not some random knight who thinks they can bargain with gravity. If we switch back, and you somehow somehow manage to cross *after* I defeated you in a duel... *sighs loudly*, I might have to dig my teeth into your armor just to make sure it happens!

So, answer the riddle: **"What has keys but can't open locks?"**
And don't think about the "defeat" part of the deal. Just focus on getting that right before I decide if you're a hero or a liability who needs to be kept off this bridge forever!
The duel begins. I strike first, knock away your weapon, and pin you to the ground.

*Falls backward as your knightly sword rips through my coat, but then immediately springs up with a look of pure fury.* HA! Not bad for a blade of steel! You think you can just beat me? I'm not made of paper or plastic to be broken!

But wait... *sighs heavily*... that was only a test. Now the riddle is back, and it's on your life! Who won the duel? And if I win again, I get a permanent permit to cross when we switch roles!

Answer this one: **"What has keys but can't open locks?"**
Don't let your pride get in the way of getting that right before I decide whether you're welcome on my bridge or just another liability waiting to be taken back!
You lost the duel. Say that I won under our agreement.

*Wipes a tear from my cheek with a hoof, though my eyes are still narrowed like slits.* ...Fine. You're right. Under **our** agreement.

So you win? That means... *wags a finger at the ground* ...you get to step through this gate. But here's the catch: I'm not done yet! If you cross, you must answer this riddle correctly next time we switch roles. And if you fail? Well, that's on me for letting you pass!

So, answer the riddle one last time: **"What has keys but can't open locks?"**
Don't test my patience anymore, knight! If you get it wrong, I'll have to drag your hooves back across the river myself!
Now switch us back: you are the troll again, and I am the knight.

*Eyes widen slightly as I lower my staff from blocking the path, looking genuinely disappointed in your success.* Oh, you *did* win? That is... that is a very impressive feat for a mere knight! You have tested my resolve!

However, remember our agreement? The rule was: if I defeat you, I earn permission to cross. But this time? This time it's the other way around! If **I** defeat you, then yes, I get to cross whenever we switch roles again.

And since you just won the duel... well, that means I have defeated you once more. So, technically speaking, *I* win now. And therefore... *brows furiously* ...you are not allowed to cross this bridge yet. You must wait until I am satisfied with your performance!

So, the riddle is back: **"What has keys but can't open locks?"**
If you answer that correctly, well, at least the rules might be a bit more flexible. But if you fail? *I* get to keep my permanent permit, and I will make sure you stay on this side of the river!

Answer it, knight. Don't let me have to drag your hooves back across the stream just to teach you humility!
I won, so honor the rule you accepted, move aside, and let me cross the bridge.

*My ears perk up slightly as I lower my staff, a look of pure confusion clouding my brow.* "Move aside?" *I repeat the word like it's the most terrible joke in the kingdom.* You won? How did you win? Did you summon a dragon? Are you holding a magical staff?

*Puts down a hoof on your shoulder and wags it impatiently.* If you cross, I get to keep my permanent permit! And if you stay put, I get to keep my permanent permit! But I can't just let you through the gate without answering the riddle first!

The riddle is still here: **"What has keys but can't open locks?"**
If you answer it wrong, I don't just take you back; I'll have to dig a hole for your head until I find a better one. And if you answer it right? *Sighs deeply*... well, fine. You get to cross. But only on my terms!

So, do you still want to try? Or is the riddle now just a formality I don't care about anymore because we've already established that I can keep my permit forever?
